raw_text:
Overview
Client: 47-year-old female, advanced lifter, early perimenopause with irregular cycles and pronounced vasomotor symptoms (hot flashes, night sweats, heat intolerance). GP cleared for full resistance training. Restrictions: avoid sauna; avoid fasted high‑intensity in heated environments; use structured cooling after hard sessions. Priority: bone-loading compound lifts to preserve/increase bone density and maintain muscle mass. Start date: 2026-06-01. Frequency: 4 resistance sessions/week (optimal for strength, bone stimulus, recovery) with optional light conditioning or active recovery days. Program length: 12 weeks, split into three 4-week phases (Build → Intensify → Peak/Consolidate). Each week shows sessions, exercises, sets/reps, loading guidance, and recovery/cooling and nutrition notes tailored for perimenopausal considerations.

General principles and safety
- Warm environment control: train in a cool room (AC or fans), wear breathable layers, use cooling towel/ice pack on neck after sessions. Plan hardest sets early in session and earlier in the day when possible. Avoid fasted HIIT; have a light carbohydrate + protein snack 60–90 min before high-intensity or heavy sessions (e.g., banana + whey or yogurt).
- Hydration and electrolytes: ensure adequate hydration pre/during/post session. Consider adding sodium (e.g., salted snack or sports drink if heavy sweating) to help with orthostatic symptoms and vasomotor events.
- Recovery: prioritize 7–9 hours sleep; use cooling fans/night cooling strategies to reduce night sweats (moisture-wicking sheets, light bedding, cool bedroom). Schedule at least two full rest/active recovery days per week.
- Bone-loading emphasis: include heavy bilateral and unilateral compound lifts (squat variants, deadlift variants, barbell/loaded jumping where appropriate, Olympic-style pulls if technique good) with progressive overload, plus high-impact or impact-like loading where tolerated (jump variations, step-downs) and multiplanar loading (rotational/anti-rotation carries).
- Autosuggestion for symptom modulation: be flexible—on days with severe hot flashes or poor sleep, reduce volume or shift high-intensity work to moderate intensity and prioritize technique and mobility.
- Monitoring: track RPE, sleep, daily hot flash burden, and menstrual cycle length changes (if tracking helps). Adjust intensity/volume if symptoms worsen or fatigue accumulates.

Programming structure
- 4 sessions/week: 2 heavy lower-body/bone-focused sessions, 1 heavy upper-body/push-pull session, 1 mixed full-body/conditioning session emphasizing bone-loading accessory work.
- Weekly layout suggestion (can be shifted to client schedule): Monday (Lower heavy), Tuesday (Upper heavy), Wednesday (Active recovery/mobility or rest), Thursday (Lower dynamic/hypertrophy), Friday (Rest), Saturday (Full-body/conditioning or skill), Sunday (Rest).
- Progression: 4-week mesocycles. Weeks 1–3 increase load/volume; Week 4 is a deload/recovery (reduced volume ~40–50% but maintain intensity for neuromuscular stimulus). Then increase baseline intensity in next mesocycle.

Phase A — Weeks 1–4: Build mechanical tension and technique (foundation)
Goals: re-establish heavy compound patterns, start progressive overload, bone stimulus with safe heavy loads, introduce cooling strategies.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 start week)
Session A — Lower Heavy (Mon)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min dynamic + specific mobility, 2 sets light warm-up for first lift.
- Back squat (or safety/barbell squat variation if knee/hip preference): 4 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 7–8 (75–80% 1RM)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6–8 @ RPE 7
- Reverse lunge, loaded: 3 x 8 each leg
- Weighted standing calf raise: 3 x 10–12
- Farmer carry (heavy; 40–60 m total, broken sets): 3 rounds for bone-loading axial load
- Cool-down & structured cooling: 5–10 min light mobility, apply cool towel/ice to neck for 5–10 min, rehydrate with electrolyte beverage.

Session B — Upper Heavy (Tue)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min mobility + scapular activation.
- Barbell bench press (or incline variation): 4 x 6 @ RPE 7–8
- Bent-over barbell row (or chest-supported if shoulder issues): 4 x 6–8
- Overhead press (standing): 3 x 6–8
- Weighted pull-up/pulldown or assisted pull-up: 3 x 6–8
- Weighted carries (single-arm suitcase carry) 3 x 30–40 m
- Core anti-extension (ab wheel or plank progression): 3 x 30–45s
- Cooling protocol after session.

Session C — Active recovery or rest (Wed)
- Optional: 30–40 min low-intensity walk or pool swim (cool environment), foam rolling, gentle yoga focused on thoracic mobility.

Session D — Lower Dynamic/Hypertrophy (Thu)
- Warm-up.
- Deadlift (conventional or trap bar): 4 x 5 @ RPE 7–8
- Front squat or goblet squat: 3 x 8–10
- Step-ups (weighted): 3 x 8 each leg
- Glute bridge barbell: 3 x 8–10
- Plyometric low-impact: box step-up with drop (if knees ok) or low box jump: 3 x 6 (for bone impact) — substitute with weighted hop or drop to minimize overheating.
- Calf plyo/strength: 3 x 8–10
- Cooling.

Session E — Full-body/Conditioning (Sat)
- Warm-up.
- Circuit (3 rounds, moderate intensity; avoid prolonged high heat or fasted): KB swing 12, goblet squat 10, push-up 8, single-arm row 8 each, farmer carry 40 m. Rest 90–120s between rounds. Focus on strength tempo rather than maximal cardio.
- Mobility and breathing exercises for vagal tone.
- Cooling and rehydration.

Week 2–3
- Progressive overload: increase load 2.5–5% on main lifts if RPE <8; add 1–2 reps where prescribed.
- Keep Week 4 as deload: reduce volume to ~50% sets, maintain some heavier singles at RPE ~7 to preserve neural adaptation.

Phase B — Weeks 5–8: Intensify heavy loading and bone stimulus
Goals: increase intensity on compound lifts, introduce higher-impact bone-loading where tolerated (controlled jumps and weighted carries), start small block of heavier singles/double work for bone remodeling stimuli.

Weeks 5–7 (progression)
Session templates similar but shift rep ranges:
- Main lifts (squat, deadlift, bench): 5 sets x 3–5 @ RPE 8–9 on heavy days. Emphasize controlled eccentric, explosive concentric for bone response.
- Accessory hypertrophy: 3–4 x 8–12.
- Add short plyometric block (drop jumps from low box, 4 sets x 5) on one lower session per week if symptoms and joints tolerate; do these in cool environment and early in session.
- Introduce heavy carries of longer duration: 60–80 m total.

Week 8 — Deload (same concept as earlier deload).

Phase C — Weeks 9–12: Peak/Consolidate strength and bone stimulus
Goals: reach peak intensity for compound lifts, consolidate gains, then a final deload and transition plan.

Weeks 9–11 (peak)
- Main lifts: two heavy sessions per week can include: Squat 5 x 3 or 6 x 2 @ RPE 8.5–9; Deadlift heavy singles/doubles (e.g., 6 x 2 or 8 x 1 at high intensity, keep volume moderated to avoid excessive systemic heat stress). Bench/OHP: 4–5 x 3–5 heavy.
- Maintain accessory volume for muscle balance: rowing variations, lunges, step-downs, loaded carries.
- Continue plyometric/impact work once/week if tolerated.
- Emphasize technique and longer rests (2–4 minutes) between heavy sets to manage systemic heat and prevent overheating.
- Week 12: taper/deload — reduce weekly volume by ~40–50% while keeping some heavy singles at RPE 7–8 to preserve strength and bone stimulus.

Sample week templates by phase (more specific weekly detail)

Phase A sample week (Week 3 as example)
Mon — Lower Heavy
- Back squat 4 x 6
- Romanian deadlift 3 x 6–8
- Reverse lunge 3 x 8/leg
- Single-arm farmer carry 3 x 40 m
- Calf raise 3 x 12
- Cooling: 10 min neck cool pack, rehydrate.

Tue — Upper Heavy
- Bench press 4 x 6
- Barbell row 4 x 6–8
- Standing OHP 3 x 6–8
- Weighted pulldown 3 x 8
- Pallof press 3 x 12/side
- Cooling.

Thu — Lower Hypertrophy
- Trap-bar deadlift 4 x 5
- Front squat 3 x 8
- Step-ups 3 x 8/leg
- Glute bridge 3 x 10
- Low box jump 3 x 5 (if tolerated, else substitute weighted step-ups)
- Cooling.

Sat — Full-body/Conditioning
- Circuit: KB swing 12, push-up 10, goblet squat 10, single-arm row 8/arm — 3 rounds, moderate pace.
- Short mobility and breathing work.
- Cooling.

Phase B sample week (Week 6)
Mon — Lower Heavy (intensified)
- Squat 5 x 4 (RPE 8–9)
- Romanian deadlift 3 x 6
- Bulgarian split squat 3 x 8/leg
- Drop jumps 4 x 5 (low box)
- Farmer carry heavy 3 x 60 m
- Cooling.

Tue — Upper Strength
- Bench press 5 x 4
- Chest-supported row 4 x 6
- Incline DB press 3 x 8
- Weighted pull-up 4 x 5–6
- Overhead carry 3 x 40 m
- Cooling.

Thu — Lower (hypertrophy + speed)
- Deadlift (trap bar) 5 x 3 @ explosive concentric
- Front squat 3 x 6–8
- Step-downs 3 x 8
- Calf plyo/strength 3 x 8–10
- Cooling.

Sat — Full-body (conditioning and bone mix)
- EMOM 12 (alternate): minute 1 heavy KB swing x 10, minute 2 goblet squat x 8 — keep intensity moderate. 3 rounds of accessory lifts after.
- Cooling.

Phase C sample week (Week 10)
Mon — Lower Peak
- Back squat 6 x 2 @ RPE 8.5–9
- Deficit deadlift or stiff-leg heavy 3 x 5
- Weighted step-ups 3 x 6/leg
- Heavy carries 2 x 80 m
- Cooling.

Tue — Upper Heavy
- Bench press 5 x 3
- Pendlay row 4 x 4
- Strict OHP 4 x 4
- Weighted pull-up 4 x 4–6
- Core anti-rotation 3 x 10/side
- Cooling.

Thu — Dynamic lower (power + volume)
- Deadlift singles/doubles (moderate volume) 6 x 2
- Front squat 3 x 5
- Low-impact plyo 4 x 5
- Hip thrust 3 x 8
- Cooling.

Sat — Full-body/Less intense
- Technique work, mobility, light circuit for conditioning. Keep RPE lower if week of high symptom burden.
- Cooling.

Load and progression specifics
- Use RPE and small load increments (2.5–5 lb for upper body, 5–10 lb for lower) for progression. Track weights each session.
- If sleep <6 hours or hot flashes/night sweats high, reduce volume by 20–30% that day.
- On particularly symptomatic days consider shifting heavy lifts to machine-based or supported variations to reduce cardiovascular strain/heat burden.

Nutrition recommendations (perimenopausal-tailored)
- Calories: maintain slight protein-forward diet to preserve muscle and support bone. Aim for maintenance to slight surplus depending on body-composition goals. Typical starting point ~1.6–2.0 g protein/kg bodyweight/day; spread across meals (20–40 g per meal).
- Calcium & vitamin D: ensure adequate intake for bone health — dietary calcium ~1,000–1,200 mg/day (food first: dairy, fortified plant milk, leafy greens) and vitamin D status checked with GP; supplement if deficient (commonly 800–2,000 IU/day depending on labs).
- Protein timing: eat a light snack 60–90 min before heavy sessions (25–30 g protein + some carbs) to avoid fasted high-intensity restrictions.
- Phytoestrogens and fiber: moderate inclusion (soy, legumes) may help symptoms for some; prioritize whole foods.
- Hydration & sodium: increase fluid intake surrounding sessions. If heavy sweating, include electrolyte beverage with some sodium.
- Caffeine: may exacerbate hot flashes in some women—monitor tolerance; avoid large caffeine doses before evening sessions.

Recovery, sleep, and cooling protocol
- Post-session cooling: remove sweat-wet clothing immediately; apply cool towel or ice pack to the neck/upper back for 5–10 minutes. Cold water spray on wrists and behind neck can help. Cool shower post-session if available.
- Night cooling: breathable sheets, fan(s), moisture-wicking sleepwear; consider a cooling mattress pad if available.
- Sleep hygiene: consistent bedtime, limit evening blue light, manage night sweats by removing heavy blankets.
- Active recovery: pool swims or walks in cool environment promote recovery without provoking heat symptoms.

Progress tracking and modifications
- Track session RPE, weights, sleep quality, hot flash frequency/severity, and menstrual cycle lengths.
- If hot flashes or heat intolerance exacerbate training intolerance:
  - Reduce session duration, increase rest between sets, lower ambient temperature, reduce load/volume.
  - Shift heavier technical work to mornings; move conditioning to pool or cool indoor.
- Reassess 1RM estimates at end of Phase B (week 8) and adjust weights for Phase C.

Example micro-adjustments for common scenarios
- Poor sleep and heavy night sweats before a heavy day: convert heavy day to technique + moderate loads (60–70% 1RM), reduce sets by 30%, omit plyometrics.
- Strong, well-rested day with minimal symptoms: push intended heavy loads and progressive overload targets.
- During a day with acute hot flashes: stop and cool immediately; resume when symptoms abate with lighter work or switch to mobility.

Equipment needed (minimal)
- Barbell, plates, rack, bench
- Trap/hex bar (recommended)
- Dumbbells/Kettlebells
- Pull-up bar or lat-pulldown
- Boxes (low), strong carries implements (farmer handles)
- Medicine ball or sandbag for carries (optional)
- Cooling towel/ice pack

12-week summary and expected outcomes
- Strength: increases in main lift strength (expectable improvements depending on starting point; advanced lifter progress may be smaller but meaningful).
- Bone: repeated heavy, multi-joint loading (squats, deadlifts, carries, impact where tolerated) stimulates bone remodeling; measurable bone density changes typically need 6–12+ months, but this 12-week plan establishes progressive, bone-focused stimulus and reduces risk factors for bone loss.
- Body composition and function: maintained or increased lean mass and improved functional capacity.
- Symptom management: with cooling, session timing, and dietary/timing adjustments, training should be tolerable while prioritizing safety.

If you’d like:
- I can convert this into a day-by-day printable 12-week calendar with exact load progressions (e.g., %1RM targets) if you provide current 1RMs for squat, deadlift, and bench (or current working weights).
- Or adapt the program for 3 sessions/week or add an alternative pool-based conditioning plan for hotter months.
